title: Chaos-driven batch/queue load prober for continuous-batching regression detection
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Goal: Create a portable, repeatable harness that stresses the runtime's continuous-batching + queueing behavior under realistic mixed workloads and injects controlled chaos (microbursts, client preemption, cache perturbation) to reveal brittle scheduling or kernel selection regressions.

Why this is different: existing load harnesses focus on steady-state or stratified arrival patterns. This prober intentionally blends long/short token sessions, priority classes, and cache-occluding traces while varying arrival processes (Poisson, bursty, bimodal) and runtime knobs (batch window, batch size soft/hard limits, kv-cache eviction). The goal is to surface subtle p95 amplifications and tokens/sec drops that only appear in continuous-batching + queueing interactions under multi-profile mixes.

Success criteria: reliable detection of p95 regressions >= 10% with statistical confidence (alpha=0.01) and clear signal-to-noise such that flaky noise is < 2% false positive rate for the environments we run on. The harness should produce reproducible heatmaps, time-series, and batch-distribution summaries and wire into regression alerting and regression IRs in Linear.
test_plan:
1) Config matrix: workloads (interactive chat short 8-128 tokens, streaming completions 256-2048 tokens, embedding/mini-batch infer 1-8 tokens per item), arrival profiles (Poisson lambda sweep, periodic microbursts, bimodal mix), tenant mixes (single-tenant heavy, multi-tenant 20 tenants with skew), KV-cache conditions (cold, warm, warmed then evicted).
2) Runtime knobs: batch window [0ms, 10ms, 25ms], max_batch_size [16, 64, 256], batch_priority_preemption enabled/disabled, kv-cache eviction aggressiveness.
3) Metrics collected: tokens_per_sec (per-GPU and cluster), p50/p95/p99 latency (generation-stage and queueing-stage split), queue_length distribution, batch_size histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate, kernel_selection path counts, GPU utilization.
4) Regression detection: rolling-window CUSUM on p95 and tokens/sec; bootstrap CI on p95 for baseline vs candidate; Mann-Whitney U for nonparametric confirmation. Alerts fire if (a) p95 increases >10% with p < 0.01 AND (b) tokens/sec drops >8% concurrently, or if p95 tail shape changes with p < 0.005.
5) Runs: nightly full-sweep on dedicated staging cluster; on-push smoke sweep for PRs changing serving runtime or kernel selector.
6) Artifact outputs: time-series (Prometheus/Grafana), batch histograms (HDF5/Parquet), reproducible input traces, deterministic seed logs.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can reproduce at least one historical regression from the last 6 months in staging (p95 headroom reduction) using the recorded seed/trace.
Automated run produces a dashboard URL and a summary JSON with p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec and triggers a Linear ticket template on regression detection.
False-positive rate measured on 30 baseline runs is <2% for p95-change alert at alpha=0.01.
results_summary: Early runs (2026-02-10..2026-02-18) on staging-nv1 showed a reproducible p95 amplification of 18% when batch_window=25ms / max_batch_size=256 with a high proportion of long-tail sessions. Tokens/sec per-GPU dropped 11% under mixed bimodal arrival vs steady Poisson baseline. KV-cache eviction scenarios amplified the effect (another +6% p95). Initial alerts correctly flagged the regression and produced a Linear automated IR (ENG-87421-R1).
decision_log:
- Scope: focus on continuous-batching logic + queue scheduling; we will not simulate full network partitions for v1.
- Detection algorithm: use CUSUM + bootstrap CI rather than relying purely on p-value thresholds to tolerate nonstationary noise.
- Integration: wire into nightly pipeline and PR checks; failures in PR checks will create a 'perf-failure' tag and require owner acknowledgment.
- Rollout plan: v1 in staging; after 2 weeks of stable baselines and tuned thresholds, enable full-sweep nightly for dedicated clusters and a lightweight PR smoke-check for runtime PRs.
notes:
Open questions: optimal seeding to balance reproducibility vs coverage (we currently store 5 seeds per scenario). Need to tune batch_window values to reflect production SLO trade-offs. We should iterate on thresholds after two weeks of telemetry.
Trade-offs: heavier chaotic perturbation finds more issues but increases false positives; mitigations include multi-run confirmation and severity bucketing.
Follow-ups: (1) add multi-model co-location scenarios in v2, (2) add particle-filter based anomaly attribution to link regressions to kernel selector path changes.
